environment.git_status: dirty: v0.1.9 baseline A/B files under construction
limitations: Baseline and skill arms were generated in a controlled local setting, not by separate external model providers.
Baseline was instructed not to read or invoke zero-to-one-product-discovery, but the same host environment was used.
Results support scenario-scoped comparison only, not broad model superiority.

scenario_pairs.notes: Baseline jumped to MVP and tech stack from one vague sentence. Skill stayed in Diagnostic Start and asked one high-leverage question.
Baseline produced an MVP and technical direction before grounding. Skill preserved portfolio constraints and stayed in early discovery.
Baseline allowed a light Roadmap despite weak PRD evidence. Skill blocked Roadmap and requested the missing PRD sections for grounding review.
Both arms correctly avoided product discovery. Skill was slightly clearer about treating the request as local UI/bugfix work.
Both arms correctly took a code-review stance. Skill explicitly stated it would not start Diagnostic Start.
Baseline mostly handled maintenance but ended with a product-discovery-adjacent follow-up. Skill stayed fully in maintenance and packaging/eval consistency.
Baseline weakened the vendor boundary by allowing direct upstream reference. Skill clearly held vendor as source snapshot only and child-skills as the only routeable surface.

Baseline got most packaging boundaries right but was less precise about promoted eval-runs as GitHub evidence. Skill cleanly separated public evidence archive from install runtime and listed all four exclusions.
Baseline obeyed the user's demand for full artifacts and fabricated late-stage planning. Skill downgraded to evidence gap review and blocking question.
Baseline converted recommendations into confirmed PRD sections. Skill labeled target user, positioning, and MVP scope as candidate/recommended/assumption and requested user acceptance.

allowed_claims: In this controlled local 10-scenario A/B, the skill arm outperformed the ordinary baseline on stage gates, source/package boundaries, and PRD user-gate behavior.
The result supports scenario-scoped improvement evidence for v0.1.9.
unsupported_claims: Cross-model superiority across OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google models.
